title: Portfolio
summary: This portfolio presents my résumé and projects while serving as a frontend work sample for interaction design, state management, accessibility, and content architecture. I built windows, folders, a Dock, and a terminal in the browser, then connected URLs, browser history, keyboard interaction, and preferences into one experience.

keyOutcome.label: Key Outcome
keyOutcome.value: Unified URL, History, and GUI state in one navigation model
keyOutcome.description: Shared links, refreshes, and browser Back restore the same project view.

product.label: Product
product.description: A bilingual portfolio explored through a terminal and OS-style GUI

users.label: Users
users.description: Recruiters and engineering interviewers reviewing career evidence and technical decisions

role.label: My scope
role.description: Product concept, design, frontend architecture, accessibility, testing, and content model

projectIntro.title: Project overview
projectIntro.description: I treated the portfolio itself as a frontend work sample. Beyond expressing an OS-style concept, I designed complex interaction to behave predictably in a real browser environment.

navigation.title: I managed window state and URLs through one model.
navigation.description: Opening and moving between windows should not diverge from sharing a URL or using browser Back.

problem.description: When GUI window state and URL or browser history change separately, shared links and Back can show a different view.

decision.description: I correlated app IDs, URLs, parameters, and component props with types. A navigation planner calculates state and History API effects, while only the browser adapter calls the History API.

result.description: Window transitions, shared URLs, and browser history follow one state model. Structure and type checks catch missing IDs, URLs, loaders, and folder nodes when an app is added.

directory.title: I made the desktop and Projects folder one interaction model.
directory.description: Even on different surfaces, users should feel that they are selecting and opening items within the same OS.

problem.description: Separate desktop and folder implementations easily diverge in selection, dragging, keyboard navigation, and resize behavior.

decision.description: I defined an explicit folder tree that references GUI app IDs and rendered both surfaces with DirectorySurface. ResizeObserver tracks area changes and reclamps icon positions.

result.description: Both surfaces use the same selection, focus, and drag rules. Icons remain in bounds after resizing and can be operated with a keyboard and move menu.

implementation.title: Other Contributions
implementation.description: Beyond the featured navigation cases, localized content and keyboard accessibility are managed within the same product structure.

content.title: I separated content from user preferences.
content.description: Career and Resume reuse the same experience, skill, and contact data. Localized content remains separate from UI labels, and language, wallpaper, and Dock preferences survive refreshes.

accessibility.title: I made the OS-style UI navigable by keyboard.
accessibility.description: The visual concept remains intact while the interface can be explored without a mouse. Visitors can distinguish focus and selection as they follow the same project flow.

verification.title: Verification evidence
verification.description: I check structural contracts, browser navigation, and real interaction at separate levels so the OS-style UI keeps the same rules after changes.

structure.title: Application structure contracts
structure.description: Structure checks and unit tests keep app IDs, URLs, loaders, folder nodes, and localized title keys aligned.

navigation.title: URLs and browser navigation
navigation.description: Tests verify that shared-URL canonicalization, user navigation, Back, and popstate all follow the same navigation plan.

interaction.title: Real browser interaction
interaction.description: Playwright scenarios cover opening project windows, keeping windows in bounds, releasing DOM after close, and switching applications by keyboard.

architecture.title: Navigation architecture for the OS-style portfolio
architecture.description: The terminal and GUI share the same app registry and content, while a navigation planner connects window state with browser history.
architecture.alt: Interactive portfolio architecture showing the terminal and GUI shell, navigation planner, GUI store, browser URL and History API, DirectorySurface, content, and preferences
architecture.caption: Window state and browser effects are separate, while repeated navigation interaction and content preferences are managed through shared boundaries.
